# cherry-pick ranges and -x: record where a patch came from

After this page you can cherry-pick one or more commits onto another branch, use a range carefully, and add a `(cherry picked from commit …)` trailer with `-x` so auditors can find the origin.

## Thesis

Merging brings a whole branch. **Cherry-pick** copies selected commits' changes as new commits on your current branch. Ranges work, but the endpoint rules differ from `log` intuition. **`-x`** appends a trailer naming the source SHA — invaluable when backporting fixes.

Verified with **git 2.47.3**.

## Lab

<!-- file: cherry-lab.sh -->
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
rm -rf /tmp/cherry-demo && mkdir /tmp/cherry-demo && cd /tmp/cherry-demo
git init -b main
git config user.name t
git config user.email t@t
git commit --allow-empty -m root
git checkout -b topic
echo a > a.txt && git add a.txt && git commit -m topic-a
echo b > b.txt && git add b.txt && git commit -m topic-b
git checkout main
git cherry-pick -x topic~1 topic
git log --oneline
git log -1 --format=%B
```

Verified output:

```text
9c9c6cb topic-b
2318a29 topic-a
ff94834 root
=== tip message ===
topic-b

(cherry picked from commit ca4a86b093b1a39397d2396080e23e5c154b7a1c)
```

The tip message includes `(cherry picked from commit …)`.

## Ranges

`git cherry-pick A..B` means commits reachable from `B` excluding those reachable from `A` — same as rev-list. To pick a single commit, pass its SHA. To pick several discrete commits, list them.

Older docs mention `A^..B` for inclusive ranges of linear history; prefer being explicit with SHAs when backporting hotfixes.

## `-x` and `-m`

- `-x` records the source commit in the message (skipped for merges unless you also pass `-m`).
- `-m parent-number` is required when cherry-picking a merge commit — choose which parent is the mainline.

## Pitfalls

1. Cherry-picking merge commits without `-m`.
2. Forgetting `-x` on backports you will need to audit later.
3. Ranges that accidentally include more commits than intended — check with `git log --oneline A..B` first.
4. Conflicts mid-sequence — finish with `--continue` / `--abort` like rebase.

## Summary

- Cherry-pick copies patches as new commits; preview ranges with `log`.
- `-x` adds provenance trailers for backports.
- Resolve conflicts with the cherry-pick continue/abort flow.


## Worked scenarios

### Scenario A — backport a single fix
```bash
git switch release/1.2
git cherry-pick -x abcdef1
git push
```

The trailer documents `abcdef1` for future audits.

### Scenario B — preview a range
```bash
git log --oneline main..topic
git cherry-pick -x main..topic   # careful: may be many commits
```

Prefer an explicit list for hotfixes.

### Scenario C — conflict mid-pick
```bash
# fix files
git add -u
git cherry-pick --continue
# or
git cherry-pick --abort
```

## Empty picks

If the changes are already present, cherry-pick may refuse empty commits unless `--skip` or `--allow-empty` — see the empty-picks stub for depth.

## Common mistakes (extended)

- Cherry-picking in the wrong direction (onto topic instead of onto release).
- Omitting `-x` on security backports.
- Ranges that include merge commits unexpectedly.
